title: KdV Hamiltonians, stationary finite gap solutions, and Lenard recursion
notes: The notes write the perturbed KdV equation, commuting integrals \(I_k\), \(H=I_{n+2}-\sum c_kI_k\), and \(\delta H/\delta u=0\); the recursion is explicitly qualified as being up to coefficients.
statement: For smooth real periodic potentials, the stationary equations of the KdV hierarchy are Euler--Lagrange equations for linear combinations of its local integrals. With suitable normalization they characterize the nonsingular finite gap potentials of genus at most \(n\). The two compatible Hamiltonian operators produce the Lenard recursion. In the displayed convention \(u_t=\partial_x(\tfrac14u_{xx}-\tfrac34u^2)\), a Hamiltonian is \(\int(-\tfrac18u_x^2-\tfrac14u^3)\,dx\).
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} Smooth periodicity, reality, and the Hamiltonian normalization have been supplied; the notebook conflates a density with its integral. The elementary identity is checked in the accompanying \nolinkurl{independent_checks.py}; this is a verification, not a novelty claim.
fate: This is background already used in \citet[pp.~1312--1313]{krichever1983hessians}; the paper distinguishes it from its new Hessian theorem.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Band edges and normalized quasimomentum
notes: For \(L=-\partial_x^2+u_0\), the notes draw \(n\) gaps and double points and give \(i\,dp=Q(E)dE/\sqrt{R(E)}\), with vanishing gap periods.
statement: For a real smooth periodic finite gap Hill operator with \(n\) open gaps, its desingularized spectral curve is \(y^2=\prod_{j=1}^{2n+1}(E-E_j)\). Its quasimomentum differential is the unique second kind differential with the prescribed principal part at infinity and zero \(a\)-periods. Its numerator has one zero in each open gap. The remaining closed gap points are double eigenvalues of the periodic or antiperiodic problems.
reconstruction: The overall factor, including the printed \(i\), depends on whether the Bloch multiplier is written as \(e^{ipT}\) or \(e^{pT}\); no normalization is silently identified across these conventions.
fate: The precise differential and periodicity constraints are recalled in \citet[pp.~1313--1314, eq.~(5)]{krichever1983hessians}; this spectral geometry predates the talk.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Spectral form of the stationary Hessian
notes: Equation (8) gives \(\delta^2H=\tfrac12\sum Q(E_i)(\delta E_i)^2+\tfrac14\sum_sQ(e_s)(\delta e_s)^2\), where \(\delta e_s\) is an opened gap width.
statement: At a stationary real finite gap potential, use Krichever\textquotesingle s normalization of \(H\) and his convention for its second variation. Let \(E_i\) be old band edges, \(e_s\) closed-gap double points, and \(\delta e_s\) the leading full widths of the newly opened gaps. Then \[\delta^2H=\frac12\sum_{i=1}^{2n+1}Q(E_i)(\delta E_i)^2+\frac14\sum_sQ(e_s)(\delta e_s)^2.\] This is a quadratic variation, not a finite-perturbation identity. The old-edge shifts satisfy the differentiated fixed-period constraints; the signs of \(Q\) therefore cannot be used to count negative directions as if all edge coordinates were independent.
reconstruction: The statement concerns the quadratic term at the stationary potential, not an exact identity for finite perturbations. The overall normalization of the hierarchy integrals must be inherited from the publication; the notebook\textquotesingle s preceding \(I_3\) normalization is inconsistent.
fate: \citet[Theorems~1--3]{krichever1983hessians} is the exact short publication: presented 19 October 1982, received 23 November 1982, published in Doklady 270(6) in 1983. Submission establishes priority before this talk, but is not evidence of public distribution.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: First order opening of a closed spectral gap
notes: The squared gap width is written as \(|\langle\delta u\,\Psi^2\rangle|^2/\langle|\Psi|^2\rangle\); the constant potential case is identified with Fourier coefficients.
statement: Let a double periodic or antiperiodic eigenvalue have an orthonormal basis \(\phi_1,\phi_2\) of its two-dimensional eigenspace. For a real perturbation \(\varepsilon v\), its two first order eigenvalue shifts are the eigenvalues of \(M_{ij}=\langle\phi_i,v\phi_j\rangle\). Thus the leading squared gap width is \(\varepsilon^2[(M_{11}-M_{22})^2+4|M_{12}|^2]\). For the free operator this becomes \(4\varepsilon^2|\widehat v(2k)|^2\) with normalized plane waves.
reconstruction: \ours{} The displayed matrix statement fixes the Hilbert-space normalization explicitly; its eigenvalue separation is checked in \nolinkurl{independent_checks.py}. Rescaling \(\Psi\) changes the notebook\textquotesingle s right side but cannot change the gap, so the formula is not correct without an unstated fixed normalization.
fate: \citet[Lemma~1 and Theorem~2]{krichever1983hessians} gives the spectral perturbation form. \ours{} The invariant two-dimensional compression is our reconstruction, which makes the missing normalization visible.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Gelfand on third and higher variations
notes: Gelfand asks: \ru{посчитать 3-ю вариацию и т.п.}
statement: At a fixed stationary finite gap potential, calculate third and higher variations of the chosen functional \(H\). A third Fr\'echet derivative in potential coordinates is well-defined once \(H\) and the function space are fixed. An analogue of the preceding spectral diagonalization requires additional choices of spectral coordinates and how a double point is unfolded.
reconstruction: The context suggests a spectral-coordinate formula, but the notes do not say that. We do not turn a request to calculate higher derivatives into an invariant open conjecture.
fate: The located exact paper concerns the Hessian and first order perturbation theory, not a general higher-variation theorem. Searches for the author, Hessians, higher/third variations, and finite gap perturbations did not identify a paper with the unspecified spectral-coordinate conclusion.
present_status: As of November 2026, ordinary higher variations are calculable from the differential-polynomial Hamiltonians; the stronger requested form cannot be identified from these notes.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Gap-opening modes and their adjoint pairing
notes: The notes expand the first order perturbation in \(w_s^\pm\), obtained by opening one additional gap, and append band-edge and divisor derivatives. They give a logarithmic theta expression and an orthogonality formula with mismatched indices.
statement: Differentiation of an exact family of KdV solutions gives a solution of the linearized equation. At a finite gap background, gap-opening modes together with tangent vectors to the finite gap family give Krichever\textquotesingle s first order perturbation expansion; squares of the corresponding Bloch solutions solve the adjoint equation and give the projections. The parameter variations must satisfy the fixed-period constraints.
reconstruction: The complete expansion includes slow variation of the background spectral parameters. The notebook\textquotesingle s single-theta formula would vanish in genus zero, although the free Fourier modes do not.
fate: \citet[Lemmas~2--3, eqs.~(13)--(19), Theorem~3]{krichever1983hessians} gives the exact basis and forced first order equations. Its mode formula uses a theta quotient with shifts \(\pm2A(e_s)\), differentiated twice, rather than the notebook\textquotesingle s logarithm of a single shifted theta function.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Shifted spectral zeta function of a Hill operator
notes: \(\zeta_{L-w}(s)=\sum(\lambda-w)^{-s}\), initially \(\Re s>1/2\); the question concerns positive integer values for a finite gap potential and spectral \(w\).
statement: For smooth real \(T\)-periodic \(u\), let \(L=-\partial_x^2+u\) have periodic or antiperiodic boundary conditions on \([0,T]\). Remove zero eigenvalues of \(L-w\) and choose a cut for negative eigenvalues when needed. The spectral series converges for \(\Re s>1/2\) and continues meromorphically. At spectral shifts the deleted zero eigenspace and boundary condition are part of the data.
reconstruction: Boundary conditions, a spectral cut, and the prime on the sum are essential additions. The short publication treats the simple and double spectra of both boundary problems.
fate: \citet[Theorems~1--2]{wodzicki1984values}, received 25 July 1983 and published in 1984, explicitly records an earlier presentation at Manin\textquotesingle s seminar in November 1982.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Hurwitz and Epstein comparisons and a binomial expansion
notes: Gelfand compares \(\sum(n+a)^{-s}\) and \(\sum(n^2+a)^{-s}\), mentions functional equations, and writes a malformed expansion.
statement: For \(a>0\), the Hurwitz zeta function is \(\zeta(s,a)=\sum_{n\ge0}(n+a)^{-s}\). For \(|a|<n^2\), \((n^2+a)^{-s}=n^{-2s}\sum_{j\ge0}(-1)^j(s)_j a^j/(j!n^{2j})\). Classical Epstein functional equations concern positive definite quadratic forms; an arbitrary homogeneous polynomial is not covered merely by homogeneity.
fate: These are older special-function comparisons, not the new finite gap theorem. The authoritative formulas for Hurwitz zeta and its continuation are collected in \citet[\S25.11]{nist2026dlmf}; the expansion also follows directly from the binomial theorem. The handwritten date 1899 is not used as a priority claim.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Arithmetic of shifted spectral values
notes: The discussion asks what happens for rational \(a\) and refers to arithmetic features of the resulting zeta series.
statement: No particular property---rationality, algebraicity, irrationality, special value, or functional equation---is fixed, and the shift and boundary conditions are not specified consistently enough to extract a single arithmetic problem.
fate: Neither the located finite gap paper nor its Lam\'e example states the blanket arithmetic question suggested by the discussion. We retain the question as unidentifiable, without attaching a famous irrationality conjecture.
present_status: As of November 2026, no definite proposition can be assigned to this wording.

title: Universal polynomials and positive integer zeta values
notes: The notes define \(F(u)=1+\sum c_i u^i/i!\), polynomial coefficients from \((u\partial_u+p)F^p\), renormalized \(\widehat Q_{p,k}\), and local derivatives of the quasimomentum; equation (4) expresses zeta values using them and Bernoulli numbers.
statement: In the finite gap setting the Taylor coefficients of the normalized quasimomentum at a branch point determine all positive integer shifted zeta values by universal polynomials. A normalization-independent computational formulation is to differentiate the regularized spectral determinant: off the spectrum, \(\partial_w^k\zeta_{L-w}\prime(0)=(k-1)!\zeta_{L-w}(k)\). At an eigenvalue, remove the appropriate zero factor before taking the finite part. The four simple/double and periodic/antiperiodic cases have different coefficients.
reconstruction: The derivative identity gives an exact modern statement without guessing ambiguous factorials in the written polynomial definition. The printed \(p=0\) convention and the power-series convention must be read together.
fate: \citet[\S2, Theorem~2 and its proof]{wodzicki1984values} gives the universal-polynomial formulas and derives them from Theorem~1. It does not support using the notebook\textquotesingle s displayed coefficients independently of its unrecorded normalization.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: The free circle and Bernoulli normalization
notes: The notes say that \(u=0,T=2\pi\) gives \(2\zeta(2s)\), then state a Bernoulli formula without the corresponding period factors.
statement: For \(-\partial_x^2\) on a circle of length \(T\), with the zero mode removed, \(\zeta_L(s)=2(T/2\pi)^{2s}\zeta_{\mathbb R}(2s)\). Consequently \(\zeta_L(m)=T^{2m}|B_{2m}|/(2m)!\) for positive integers \(m\). In particular, at \(T=2\pi\) the factor is \((2\pi)^{2m}\), not \(2^{2m}\).
reconstruction: \oursComputed{}  The elementary identity is checked in the accompanying \nolinkurl{independent_checks.py}; this is a verification, not a novelty claim.
fate: This is the elementary free check of the formulas in \citet[Theorem~2]{wodzicki1984values}; Euler\textquotesingle s value formula is given in \citet[\S25.6]{nist2026dlmf}.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: One-gap Lamé quasimomentum
notes: For \(u=2\wp(x)\), the notes write a cubic spectral curve, a Weierstrass-zeta Bloch exponent, and a quasimomentum differential.
statement: Choose a real nonsingular periodic translate \(u(x)=2\wp(x+x_0)\). If the elliptic curve for \(\wp\) is \(y^2=4\prod(z-e_i)\), the Hill spectral curve uses \(E=-z\), hence its branch points are \(-e_i\). The Bloch exponent is obtained from \(T\zeta(a)-\eta a\), with \(\wp(a)=-E\), and the differential and zeta values follow after this coordinate change.
reconstruction: The real-axis translate avoids poles. A \(+g_3\) in the spectral cubic and a \(-g_3\) in the Weierstrass cubic are compatible under \(E=-z\); the sign is not automatically a transcription error.
fate: \citet[\S4]{wodzicki1984values} explicitly distinguishes the Weierstrass curve from the reflected spectral curve and gives the simple and double spectral values.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Multiplicativity of the zeta determinant
notes: Gelfand asks whether regularized determinants of differential operators are multiplicative.
statement: For commuting, positive, invertible, classical elliptic pseudodifferential operators \(A,B\) of positive orders \(a,b\), on a closed smooth manifold and on the same Hermitian vector bundle, define \(\det_\zeta A=\exp[-\zeta_A\prime(0)]\). In general \(\det_\zeta(AB)\ne\det_\zeta A\det_\zeta B\). In this commuting positive setting the logarithmic anomaly is \[\frac{\operatorname{res}\bigl(\log(A^bB^{-a})\bigr)^2}{2ab(a+b)}.\] Noncommuting or nonpositive operators require the appropriate more general formula and compatible admissible cuts.
fate: \citet[\S1.1]{kontsevichvishik1994geometry} explains the anomaly and the spectral-cut hypotheses; its June 1994 preprint is an abridgement of their April 1994 work. The commuting formula is explicitly stated with its hypotheses in \citet[eq.~(1)]{castillogarate2015anomaly}.
present_status: As of November 2026, general multiplicativity is false. Local residue anomaly formulas and special vanishing classes are established; there is no remaining blanket conjecture here.

title: Euler, Apéry, and regularized sums
notes: The discussion mentions Euler\textquotesingle s even values, Ap\'ery\textquotesingle s \(\zeta(3)\), and assigns values to \(\sum n^2\), \(\sum n^3\).
statement: Euler\textquotesingle s formula is \(\zeta(2m)=(-1)^{m+1}B_{2m}(2\pi)^{2m}/[2(2m)!]\). Ap\'ery proved that \(\zeta(3)\) is irrational. Analytic continuation gives \(\zeta(-2)=0\) and \(\zeta(-3)=1/120=-B_4/4\); these are zeta-regularized values, not sums of convergent positive-term series.
fate: \citet{apery1979irrationalite} published the irrationality proof in 1979, before the talk. The continuation identities are recorded in \citet[\S25.6]{nist2026dlmf}.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: The D-module sketch for a complex power
notes: A short diagram separates integer and noninteger exponents of \(x^{-s}\), with arrows and subquotients.
statement: On the punctured complex line, \(x^{-s}\) generates the rank-one connection \((x\partial_x+s)f=0\) with monodromy \(e^{-2\pi i s}\). At integral exponents, extensions across zero can have punctual subquotients. A specific extension functor or module presentation is needed to identify the diagram.
reconstruction: The rank-one connection is supplied only to locate the subject. It is not an assertion that the diagram equals a specified minimal or maximal extension.
fate: The local connection is an elementary reconstruction; the notebook does not specify the extension or its arrows sufficiently to match an exact module theorem. No fate is inferred from a general reference on D-modules.
present_status: As of November 2026, the local connection is standard; the displayed extension diagram remains unidentifiable.

title: Clausen series and a negative-even zeta derivative
notes: The notes express \(\zeta_{L-w}\prime(-2)\) using Clausen functions and branch-count corrections; they write \(\operatorname{Cl}_5(0)=\zeta(-5)\).
statement: With \(\operatorname{Cl}_{2k+1}(\theta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\cos(n\theta)/n^{2k+1}\), one has \(\operatorname{Cl}_5(0)=\zeta(5)\). For the free circle, \(\zeta_L\prime(-2)=48\zeta(5)/T^4\), obtained by differentiating \(2(T/2\pi)^{2s}\zeta(2s)\). The general shifted formula needs the spectral branch and the counting function for negative eigenvalues.
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} Only the explicitly checked free specialization and the definition of the Clausen function are asserted here.
fate: The located Wodzicki paper proves positive integer values, not the entire Clausen expression on this page. The free specialization follows from \citet[\S25.4]{nist2026dlmf}; the complete displayed identity has not been verified in an exact source.
present_status: As of November 2026, the free specialization is established; the full recorded branch-sensitive formula remains unverified.

title: A closed one-form as a many-valued action
notes: The action is \(S=S_0+S_1\), where local \(q\)-form primitives of a closed \((q+1)\)-form define \(S_1\). The variation is asserted to be single-valued.
statement: Let \(N\) be a closed oriented smooth \(q\)-manifold and \(\Omega\in\Omega^{q+1}(M)\) closed. On the smooth mapping space the transgression \(\alpha_\phi(v)=\int_N\phi^*(\iota_v\Omega)\) is a closed one-form. Locally it is the derivative of an action; its periods are integrals of \(\Omega\) over the cycles swept out by loops of maps. Adding a single-valued functional \(S_0\) does not change this period obstruction.
reconstruction: Closedness and orientation of the source, and the transgression formula, are explicit modern hypotheses. The notebook does not develop a complete differential-cohomology model.
fate: \citet[\S5]{novikov1982hamiltonian} gives the many-valued functional construction. It was received 22 April 1982 and published in 1982, before this March 1983 exposition.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Dirac monopole and the phase of the action
notes: The example takes \(N=S^1\), \(M=S^2\), and a closed two-form that is not globally exact.
statement: For the magnetic two-form of a monopole on \(S^2\), local magnetic potentials give a multi-valued action on loops. The curvature can have a global primitive only if its integral over \(S^2\) vanishes. If the transgression periods lie in \(2\pi\mathbb Z\), exponentiating the action gives a single-valued phase on the chosen component, after a reference normalization.
fate: \citet[\S\S4--5]{novikov1982hamiltonian} explicitly treats the Dirac monopole and the resulting multivalued action. The integral-period phase formulation is a reconstruction of the obstruction, not a separate theorem claimed from the seminar.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Local actions and constant transition differences
notes: The notes choose primitive patches \(U_\alpha\) in \(M\), use maps whose entire images lie in one patch, and say \(S_\alpha-S_\beta\) is constant. A tentative Witten/chiral-field reference follows.
statement: On an overlap of mapping-space domains where two local actions have the same derivative, their difference is constant on each connected component. Domains consisting of maps into one primitive patch need not cover the entire mapping space; a general construction uses local homotopies to reference maps or subdivisions. The chiral-field attribution does not state a further definite claim.
reconstruction: Locally constant replaces globally constant on a disconnected overlap. The tentative attribution is retained as a bibliographic lead, not an exact later solution.
fate: \citet[\S5, the local-action construction]{novikov1982hamiltonian} explains why the variations agree. The scope repair follows from the closed transgression form, without asserting that every map fits into one target chart.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Double Lie algebras and invariant Hamiltonians
notes: \([X,Y]_R=[RX,Y]+[X,RY]\) is required to be a Lie bracket; invariant functions commute for both associated brackets, and their Hamiltonian equation has a Lax form. The heading cites Drinfeld, Doklady volume 268, no.5, under the words Lie bialgebra.
statement: If a linear map \(R:\mathfrak g\to\mathfrak g\) makes \([\ ,\ ]_R\) a Lie bracket, the two brackets define Lie--Poisson structures on \(\mathfrak g^*\). Adjoint-invariant smooth functions are in involution for both. For such \(h\), the second Hamiltonian vector field is \(\dot L=\operatorname{ad}^*_{R\,dh(L)}L\), with the coadjoint sign convention fixed consistently. A double Lie algebra alone is not the same datum as a Lie bialgebra.
reconstruction: Finite dimensionality is sufficient for the stated differential-geometric formulation; infinite-dimensional examples require a specified pairing and domains.
fate: \citet{semenov1983classical} was received 15 April 1983, revised 16 May, and published in volume 17(4) later in 1983; this is a publication after the March talk, not evidence that the theorem was new on that evening. The exact result is \citet[\S1, Theorem~1; \S2]{semenov1983classical}. The distinct bibliographic pointer is \citet[\S4, Theorem~2]{drinfeld1983hamiltonian}, which defines a Lie bialgebra by a cobracket satisfying the one-cocycle compatibility, equivalently a compatible invariant double on \(\mathfrak g\oplus\mathfrak g^*\). Its actual issue is268(2), pages 285--287, received 4 June 1982 and published 1983. This background is not the same assertion as the operator double Lie algebra in the talk.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Modified Yang–Baxter equation, the double, and factorization
notes: The defect \([RX,RY]-R([RX,Y]+[X,RY])\) is set equal to \(-[X,Y]\). The maps \(R\pm1\), a decomposition in the double, and the factorization of \(\exp(t\,dh)\) are used to integrate the flow.
statement: The modified identity implies that \(R\pm I:\mathfrak g_R\to\mathfrak g\) are Lie homomorphisms. Their joint image in \(\mathfrak g\oplus\mathfrak g\) is complementary to the diagonal. In the corresponding local groups, the factorization problem, with its common-quotient constraint, is locally soluble. For the unhalved bracket used here, the exponential is \(\exp(2t\,dh(L_0))\); the resulting coadjoint action integrates the invariant Hamiltonian flow.
reconstruction: Global factorization is not automatic. The notebook omits the quotient compatibility when the two images intersect and loses the factor of two associated with its bracket convention.
fate: \citet[\S\S3--4, Proposition~9 and Theorem~11, eq.~(18)]{semenov1983classical} gives the exact local result, including the factor \(2\). \citet{semenov1983classical} was received 15 April 1983, revised 16 May, and published in volume 17(4) later in 1983; this is a publication after the March talk, not evidence that the theorem was new on that evening.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Gelfand’s classification problem for sl(2)
notes: Gelfand asks to find all \(R\) satisfying the displayed modified Yang--Baxter equation on \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\).
statement: Over \(\mathbb C\), classify all linear maps \(R\) satisfying \([Rx,Ry]-R([Rx,y]+[x,Ry])=-[x,y]\), modulo Lie-algebra automorphisms. No skew-adjoint restriction is imposed by the question. Writing \(B=(R-I)/2\) identifies this exactly with Rota--Baxter operators of weight one: \([Bx,By]=B([Bx,y]+[x,By]+[x,y])\).
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} The ground field and equivalence relation are supplied. Real forms require a separate classification, which the notebook does not select. The elementary identity is checked in the accompanying \nolinkurl{independent_checks.py}; this is a verification, not a novelty claim.
fate: An explicit classification and proof are in \citet[Proposition~2.5 and its proof]{gubarevkozlov2023rota}; its source cases are closed under conjugacy and the involution \(B\mapsto-B-I\), with \(0,-I\) included separately. Received September 2022, published 2023. This answers the complex operator problem without replacing it by the narrower skew tensor problem. With \([h,e]=2e\), \([h,f]=-2f\), \([e,f]=h\), representative weight-one operators are \(B(e)=-e,B(f)=B(h)=0\); \(B(e)=-(e+h),B(f)=B(h)=0\); and \(B(e)=-e,B(f)=0,B(h)=th\), \(t\ne0\), together with \(0,-I\), conjugacy and \(B\mapsto-I-B\).
present_status: As of November 2026, the complex finite-dimensional operator classification is established. The primary proof was read; this item does not claim a new classification.

title: Quadratic Poisson bracket and the Hamiltonian hierarchy
notes: A quadratic bracket with terms \(R(XL)\) and \(R(LX)\) is followed by a hierarchy of invariant Hamiltonians.
statement: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be an associative algebra with nondegenerate symmetric invariant trace pairing, and let \(R\) be skew with respect to it and satisfy the modified Yang--Baxter equation. Then the quadratic bracket of Semenov-Tian-Shansky\textquotesingle s equation (22) is Poisson and compatible with the linear \(R\)-bracket. Invariant functions commute for it, and trace powers produce the associated Lenard hierarchy. In formal pseudodifferential examples the trace is the integrated formal residue and the differential/negative-order splitting supplies \(R\).
reconstruction: Skew-adjointness, the trace pairing and associative multiplication are needed for the particular theorem verified here; the bare assumption that the linear \(R\)-bracket satisfies Jacobi is insufficient.
fate: \citet[\S5, Theorem~13 and eqs.~(22)--(23)]{semenov1983classical} gives precisely these hypotheses. This is related to earlier Gelfand--Dikii discussions (1977-426.5 and 1977-426.10), but not an exact recurrence of the earlier question about the first bracket.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Spectral boundary conditions and the APS index formula
notes: For \(D=\partial_u+A\) near the boundary, the projector onto the nonnegative spectrum of self-adjoint \(A\) is imposed; the index is \(\int_X\alpha_0-(h+\eta(0))/2\).
statement: Let a Dirac-type elliptic operator on a compact manifold with boundary have product structure in a collar, with self-adjoint tangential operator \(A\). Impose \(P_{\ge0}(A)(s|_{\partial X})=0\). The realization is Fredholm and \(\operatorname{ind}D_{APS}=\int_X\alpha_0-(\eta_A(0)+\dim\ker A)/2\). The normal bundle isomorphism in the usual Dirac decomposition is suppressed in the notes.
fate: \citet[Theorem~3.10 and \S4]{atiyahpatodisinger1975spectral1} is the exact pre-talk source (received March 1974, published 1975). This repeats 1981-558.11--12 and 1981-559.2.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Replacing self-adjointness by a spectral-cut hypothesis
notes: The notes say self-adjointness may be replaced by absence of spectrum near the imaginary axis.
statement: Complex powers of a general elliptic classical operator require an Agmon ray: the ray avoids both the nonzero principal-symbol eigenvalues and the operator spectrum. For boundary problems the corresponding sectorial projection must also define an elliptic boundary condition. Avoiding the imaginary axis only at the level of the discrete global spectrum does not supply these microlocal hypotheses.
reconstruction: The statement separates the established spectral-cut calculus from a blanket boundary Fredholm theorem, which the one-line remark does not formulate.
fate: The non-self-adjoint closed-operator calculus was already available in \citet[pp.~96--98]{seeley1968powers}, a 1968 Russian translation explicitly identified as a preprint. It requires the principal-symbol ray condition, constructs complex powers and meromorphic diagonal kernels, and gives the shifted-zeta index identity. \citet[\S1]{kontsevichvishik1994geometry} restates admissibility precisely. Wodzicki\textquotesingle s \citet{wodzicki1982spectral} is also pre-talk, but only publisher metadata was checked. This is the earlier problem GP-1981-44; the shorthand about boundary projections does not by itself state a complete boundary theorem.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Fedosov’s idempotents for an elliptic symbol
notes: Fedosov constructs a matrix projector from cutoffs \(f_1,f_2\) and \(\sigma,\sigma^*\), then gives a pair \(P_1,P_2\) for general bundles.
statement: An elliptic symbol \(\sigma:\pi^*E_1\to\pi^*E_2\), invertible away from the zero section, defines a compactly supported \(K^0(T^*X)\) class. In a unitary trivialization the block matrix \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}f_1^2&f_1f_2\sigma\\f_1f_2\sigma^*&f_2^2\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) is an idempotent when \(\sigma\sigma^*=I\) and \(f_1^2+f_2^2=1\). For the later nonorthogonal idempotent pair, the auxiliary symbol and its parametrix must be mutual inverses outside a compact set for their difference to represent a compactly supported class.
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} The algebraic projector identities and the support condition are separate issues. We do not assert that the later pair fails idempotence; the potential error is its cutoff behavior at infinity. The elementary identity is checked in the accompanying \nolinkurl{independent_checks.py}; this is a verification, not a novelty claim.
fate: The symbol-class and Chern-character framework is the classical index construction described in \citet[Chapter~3]{gilkey1984invariance}. The written projector identities were checked directly; the exact displayed cutoff formula was not attributed to an independently located Fedosov paper.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.
speaker: B. V. Fedosov

title: Chern character, Todd form, and the symbol index
notes: The displayed integral is a difference of traces of \(P_i\exp(\omega_i/2\pi i)\) multiplied by the Todd class; \(\omega_i=P_i dP_i dP_i\).
statement: For smooth idempotents representing a compactly supported symbol class, the Grassmann connection has curvature \(P(dP)^2\). Its Chern character difference is paired with \(\pi^*\operatorname{Td}(T_\mathbb C X)\), using the cotangent orientation and the conventional index sign, to obtain the analytic index. Curvature normalization and complexification matter in comparing \(R/(e^R-1)\) with \(R/(1-e^{-R})\).
reconstruction: The support, orientation and curvature conventions have been supplied; the notebook\textquotesingle s two Todd conventions are not treated as an unambiguous sign error.
fate: This is classical topological index theory; \citet[Chapter~3]{gilkey1984invariance} supplies the Chern--Weil formulation. No new universal Todd identity is inferred from the crossed-out curvature notation.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.
speaker: B. V. Fedosov

title: Index from shifted zeta functions and local parametrices
notes: Wodzicki sets \(DD^*=\Delta_2\), \(D^*D=\Delta_1\), writes an index difference of shifted zeta values, and a local symbol integral for \(\alpha_0\).
statement: On a closed manifold, \(\operatorname{ind}D=\zeta_{D^*D+1}(0)-\zeta_{DD^*+1}(0)\), because the positive spectra cancel and each zero mode becomes the eigenvalue one. For a positive elliptic differential operator \(A\), \(\zeta_A(0)\) with zero modes removed equals its integrated constant heat coefficient minus \(\dim\ker A\). Resolvent-symbol contour integrals compute the heat coefficients, with an admissible cut and the chosen Fourier normalization.
reconstruction: The exact shifted identity concerns a closed elliptic problem, or paired boundary realizations with the required spectral cancellation. A generic pseudodifferential heat expansion may include logarithmic terms, so the differential-operator hypothesis is retained.
fate: \citet[\S1.10 and Chapter~3]{gilkey1984invariance} gives the heat/zeta formulation. This is a recurrence of 1981-558.3--4, 1981-559.10--11; the first argument on the scan is an ambiguous crossed zero, not a new parameter. The exact shifted spectral cancellation is already written in \citet[p.~98]{seeley1968powers}, attributed there to Atiyah and Bott.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Local index densities for signature and Dirac operators
notes: The notebook says the local density agrees with the topological formula for signature and Dirac operators and mentions equivariant versions.
statement: For geometric signature and Dirac-type complexes on a closed Riemannian manifold, the supertrace heat-kernel constant term is the appropriate characteristic-form density, with the twisting Chern character when present. For an orientation-preserving compact-group symmetry preserving the operator data, the equivariant index is described by fixed-point local contributions.
fate: The pre-talk local index theorem is proved in \citet{atiyahbottpatodi1973heat}; \citet[Chapter~3]{gilkey1984invariance} provides the corresponding invariant-theoretic treatment. This repeats 1981-558.1 and 1981-558.7.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Formal cohomology of metrics and symbols
notes: Gelfand proposes calculating formal cohomology for the metric and the symbol and asks whether classes other than the index occur; Gelfand--Fuks cohomology and maximal topological invariants are mentioned.
statement: The note does not specify the Lie algebra of formal coordinate changes, coefficient module, equivalence relation on symbols, or degree. Those choices distinguish Chern--Weil invariant polynomials, local scalar invariants, and Gelfand--Fuks cohomology, so no single formal-cohomology calculation is determined.
fate: \citet[\S\S2.4--2.6]{gilkey1984invariance} classifies specified local invariant problems; it is thematic evidence, not a solution of the unspecified combined metric-and-symbol problem.
present_status: As of November 2026, no definite open question can be extracted without choosing the formal complex.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Signature defect and equivariant eta series
notes: The signature formula is \(\operatorname{sign}X=\int_XL-\eta(0)\); an equivariant eta series inserts \(\operatorname{Tr}(g|E_\lambda)\).
statement: For a compact oriented \(4k\)-manifold with product metric near its boundary, the APS signature theorem expresses the signature as the integral of the Hirzebruch \(L\)-form minus the eta invariant of the boundary odd signature operator in the APS convention. If \(g\) is a symmetry commuting with the self-adjoint tangential operator, \(\eta_A(s,g)=\sum_{\lambda\ne0}\operatorname{sign}(\lambda)\operatorname{Tr}(g|E_\lambda)|\lambda|^{-s}\) initially converges in a right half-plane.
reconstruction: The signature normalization differs from the general index expression with \((\eta+h)/2\); its kernel convention cannot simply be interchanged.
fate: \citet[\S4]{atiyahpatodisinger1975spectral1} gives the signature theorem; the boundary operator uses the Hodge star, not merely the formal adjoint of \(d\). This continues 1981-558.8.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Eta regularity without a bounding manifold
notes: Part III is summarized as regularity of \(\eta(0)\) in odd dimension without requiring the operator to be a boundary operator.
statement: For a self-adjoint classical elliptic operator of positive order on a closed smooth manifold, the global eta function is regular at zero. APS III proves the odd-dimensional result by its topological argument; the general-dimensional theorem does not imply that the local eta residue density vanishes pointwise.
fate: \citet[Theorem~4.5]{atiyahpatodisinger1976spectral3} proves the odd-dimensional statement (received January 1975, published 1976). \citet[Theorem~0.1]{gilkey1981residue} proves the general statement before this 1983 talk. This settles the exact earlier problem GP-1981-43.
present_status: As of November 2026, the global eta-regularity question is settled; local residue assertions require separate hypotheses.

title: Flat bundles, secondary K-theory, and reduced eta
notes: A unitary representation of \(\pi_1X\), a class with \(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\) coefficients, and a map to \(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\) are drawn next to the symbol class.
statement: A rank-\(n\) flat unitary bundle defines a secondary class relative to the trivial rank-\(n\) bundle. Pairing an appropriate \(K\)-theory class with it gives a secondary index in \(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\), represented analytically by the difference of reduced eta invariants \(\bar\eta(A_E)-n\bar\eta(A)\) modulo integers. The base class lies on \(X\); its product with a compactly supported cotangent symbol is formed only after pullback.
reconstruction: Reduced eta means \((\eta(0)+\dim\ker)/2\). We supply the rank subtraction and distinguish a class on the base from its pullback to the cotangent bundle.
fate: \citet[\S\S4.3--4.4]{gilkey1984invariance} gives the secondary-index and eta interpretation of APS theory. The notebook\textquotesingle s diagram is schematic; the exact coefficient grading is not recoverable from its arrows alone.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Loops, Hardy polarization, and the restricted Grassmannian
notes: \(H^{(n)}=L^2(S^1,\mathbb C^n)=H_+\oplus H_-\), \(W_\gamma=\gamma H_+\); the positive projection is Fredholm and the negative one compact. The Grassmannian is compared with \(\Omega U(n)\).
statement: For a continuous invertible matrix loop \(\gamma\), multiplication on \(L^2\) is bounded invertible, \(W_\gamma\) is closed, and its Hardy projections have the stated properties. The full restricted Grassmannian is larger than the loop orbit. The subspace with \(zW\subset W\) is the appropriate loop Grassmannian; continuous based unitary loops inject into a dense subspace of it, with a completion admitting measurable loops.
fate: \citet[\S2, Proposition~2.7 and the following discussion]{segalwilson1985loop} states the continuous-loop inclusion and the distinction between the completed Grassmannian and \(\Omega U(n)\). \citet{segalwilson1985loop} develops the joint work reported here; publication was in 1985. The present seminar notes themselves document circulation in March--April 1983.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Which measurable loops give the Fredholm and compact projections?
notes: The notes call it an unsolved problem to characterize all loops for which conditions (i) and (ii) hold.
statement: For continuous invertible loops the conditions already hold. A precise wider version takes an essentially bounded unitary matrix loop \(\gamma\). Then \(W_\gamma\to H_+\) is Fredholm and \(W_\gamma\to H_-\) compact exactly when the matrix entries lie in \(QC=(H^\infty+C)\cap\overline{H^\infty+C}\). Indeed Hartman\textquotesingle s theorem identifies compact Hankel blocks; the Toeplitz block is essentially unitary exactly when both off-diagonal blocks are compact.
reconstruction: We explicitly restrict the reconstruction to essentially bounded unitary loops. \ours{} Write the unitary multiplier as \(U=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{smallmatrix}\right)\). If \(c\) is compact, then \(a^*a=1\) in the Calkin algebra; Fredholmness makes \(a\) invertible there, whence \(aa^*=1\) and \(bb^*=0\), so \(b\) is compact. Conversely compact \(b,c\) make \(a\) unitary modulo compacts and hence Fredholm. Hartman\textquotesingle s criterion then gives \(QC\) entrywise.
fate: \citet[pp.~221--223]{page1975compact} proves the compact-Hankel characterization (Hartman\textquotesingle s theorem dates to 1958). \ours{} The unitary-loop equivalence is the elementary block-operator consequence checked here. The notes do not specify this ambient measurable class, so no unresolved general \(GL_n\) loop problem is asserted.
present_status: As of November 2026, the unitary measurable reconstruction has the stated classical criterion. The literal phrase all loops lacks a function class.

title: Grassmannian flows and Krichever’s algebro-geometric locus
notes: The notes map a Grassmannian to solutions of the \(n\)th KdV hierarchy and place the Krichever construction inside it, followed by a dressing-method comparison.
statement: For scalar polarized \(L^2(S^1)\), the reduction \(z^nW\subset W\) yields an order-\(n\) scalar differential Lax operator and its Gelfand--Dikii flows. General Grassmannian points give KP. The algebro-geometric construction supplies a distinguished locus, and polynomial/rational finite-dimensional approximations are dense in the relevant Grassmannian topology; this is not a classification of all solutions of arbitrary growth.
reconstruction: The reduction and analytic class delimit the word solutions; no universal surjectivity onto every smooth KdV initial value is inferred.
fate: \citet[\S\S2,5--7]{segalwilson1985loop} verifies the reduction and its algebraic loci. \citet{segalwilson1985loop} develops the joint work reported here; publication was in 1985. The present seminar notes themselves document circulation in March--April 1983.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Modified hierarchies and the Miura flag
notes: A commutative diagram relates a flag manifold to modified KdV and the Grassmannian to KdV; the Miura fibre is written \(G/B\).
statement: For a local monic scalar differential operator of order \(n\), factorizations into first order operators correspond to suitable complete flags in its local solution space. The Miura transformation carries modified hierarchy solutions to the ordinary hierarchy. Analytic factorizations near an ordinary point form the open set of flags with nonvanishing required Wronskians; allowing meromorphic factors recovers the full flag variety.
reconstruction: Local solution fields and meromorphic versus analytic factorizations are distinguished; global periodic fibres need not equal a single flag variety.
fate: \citet[\S3.7 and \S6]{drinfeldsokolov1985lie} develops the Miura transformation and generalized hierarchies; its introduction identifies the 1981 Doklady announcement as the earlier source. Thus this is pre-talk mathematics despite the 1984 Russian/1985 English survey publication.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Determinant lines, affine central extensions, and tau
notes: The tau function is introduced as a determinant, with an affine Lie-algebra extension and a theta-function special case.
statement: The determinant line over the index-zero restricted Grassmannian produces a tau function after an admissible frame and a lift of the positive loop action are chosen. The restricted linear group acts through a central extension; on smooth matrix loops its infinitesimal cocycle is a scalar multiple of \((2\pi i)^{-1}\oint\operatorname{tr}(X\,dY)\). The scalar tau function is not canonically independent of all trivializations.
fate: \citet[\S\S3--4 and 10]{segalwilson1985loop} gives the determinant construction and central extension. The affine algebra itself was older; the specific analytic tau model is the joint work announced here.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Krichever’s KP zero-curvature and tau reconstruction
notes: Krichever replaces commuting ordinary operators by compatible \(\partial_y-L\), \(\partial_t-L_1\), and writes \(u=-2\partial_x^2\log\tau\) for \(L=-\partial_x^2+u\).
statement: For a KP auxiliary system, the compatibility condition is \([\partial_y-L,\partial_t-L_1]=0\). In the convention \(L=-\partial_x^2+u\), the potential reconstructed from tau is \(u=-2\partial_x^2\log\tau\), up to any explicitly chosen constant background. The sign reverses for the standard monic \(\partial_x^2+u\) convention.
reconstruction: The relation is a compatibility equation in two evolution variables, not ordinary commutativity of time-dependent \(L,L_1\).
fate: \citet[\S5, especially eq.~(5.19)]{segalwilson1985loop} gives the monic convention and its tau reconstruction. The notebook\textquotesingle s sign is consistent with its negative leading term.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.
speaker: I. M. Krichever

title: Index-zero Grassmannian and admissible frames
notes: The restricted Grassmannian is defined by Fredholm/compact projections. Frames \(w:H_+\to W\) have \(w_+=I+\text{trace class}\), \(w_-\) compact; the text says all points have such frames.
statement: The Fredholm index labels the connected components of the restricted Grassmannian. The stated frame condition parametrizes the index-zero component. For \(g\in\Gamma_+\), holomorphic and nonvanishing on a neighbourhood of the closed disc, choose its block decomposition \(g^{-1}=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&b\\0&d\end{smallmatrix}\right)\). The trace-class block needed for the determinant is available in this analytic loop class.
reconstruction: The scan first notes the full Grassmannian, with all Fredholm indices, and also displays the index-zero qualification. The later frame construction is interpreted on that index-zero component; the unrestricted assertion about every point would be false.
fate: \citet[\S\S2--3]{segalwilson1985loop} gives the component and frame construction. \citet{segalwilson1985loop} develops the joint work reported here; publication was in 1985. The present seminar notes themselves document circulation in March--April 1983.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: The Fredholm determinant tau function and its zero set
notes: \(\tau_W(g)=\det(w_++a^{-1}bw_-)\); transversality is stated as both invertibility of the positive projection and \(W\cap H_-=0\).
statement: On the index-zero component, the operator inside the determinant is identity plus trace class, so its Fredholm determinant is defined. Its vanishing is equivalent to failure of \(g^{-1}W\to H_+\) to be invertible. There, injectivity is equivalent to invertibility because the index is zero. On the big cell the graph frame gives \(\tau_W(1)=1\); elsewhere this normalization is unavailable.
reconstruction: An arbitrary Fredholm operator has no ordinary determinant. The frame normalization and trace-class subtraction are essential.
fate: \citet[\S3, determinant-line discussion]{segalwilson1985loop} gives this construction.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Nonvanishing, Schur functions, and Plücker coefficients
notes: The tau function is never identically zero, even on \(g=e^{xz}\). Coordinate subspaces \(H_S\) give Schur functions, and general tau has a Pl\"ucker-coordinate expansion.
statement: For an index-zero Grassmannian point, \(\tau_W(t)=\sum_S w^S F_S(t)\), where \(F_S\) is the Schur function associated with the charge-zero indexing set \(S\), with the sign convention determined by \(g^{-1}\). For \(t=(x,0,\ldots)\), the leading power has nonzero coefficient and degree equal to the codimension of the stratum containing \(W\). Schur functions also encode polynomial \(GL_n\) characters after a finite-variable specialization.
reconstruction: The coefficient conventions use the charge-zero partition, not an arbitrary increasing set without its eventual indexing condition.
fate: \citet[Propositions~8.2--8.3 and 8.6]{segalwilson1985loop} proves the expansion and the stronger one-variable nonvanishing. The representation-theoretic identification answers the brief \(GL(n)\) aside.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: The Krichever map and its Fredholm index
notes: A pointed curve, a disc at infinity, a line bundle (rank-one torsion-free sheaf for a singular curve), and a trivialization produce \(W\); the index is \(\chi(\mathcal L)-1\).
statement: Let \(X\) be an integral complete algebraic curve, smooth at a marked point \(p\), with a local coordinate and a trivialized rank-one torsion-free sheaf \(\mathcal L\) near \(p\). The closure of boundary values of sections on the complement defines a Grassmannian point. With \(H_+=\operatorname{span}\{1,z,z^2,\ldots\}\) and \(z\) a pole coordinate at \(p\), the projection index is \(\chi(\mathcal L(-p))=\chi(\mathcal L)-1\).
reconstruction: The coordinate, local freeness at the marked point, and boundary-value completion are supplied. Genus and degree need not be guessed from the index.
fate: \citet[\S6, Proposition~6.1]{segalwilson1985loop} is the exact analytic realization of the older Krichever construction.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Theta factorization of an algebro-geometric tau function
notes: The notes relate \(\Gamma_+\) to \(H^1(X,\mathcal O)\) and write \(\tau=e^{\alpha_{W,0}+Q}\theta(\bar f-\beta_W)\), with \(Q\) depending only on the curve and disc.
statement: For a smooth pointed curve with fixed local coordinate and line-bundle data, the Krichever tau function is a theta function on its Jacobian composed with the linear map from flow times, multiplied by an exponential with linear and quadratic terms. The quadratic form is determined by the pointed curve and normalization; the line bundle changes the translate and the linear factor.
fate: \citet[\S9, especially Theorem~9.11]{segalwilson1985loop} gives the exact theta comparison. This continues the curve-based theta constructions indexed in 1977-431.3.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Gelfand’s request for theta functions of all abelian varieties
notes: \ru{Построить теорию интегрирования, связанную с \(\theta\)-функцией \(\forall\) абелевых многообразий}; the parenthesis says only Jacobians of curves occur here.
statement: The notes ask for an integration theory attached to arbitrary abelian varieties but do not specify equations, a notion of integrability, or a universal construction. The exact Jacobian theta solution of KP is a different, narrower statement.
fate: The exact curve construction is in \citet[\S9]{segalwilson1985loop}. \citet{shiota1986characterization} is a later Jacobian-characterization reference, not a solution of the all-abelian-varieties programme; only its publisher metadata and bibliography were checked here. That bibliography records 1983 Kyoto seminar notes separately from the 1986 publication.
present_status: As of November 2026, this broad programme does not specify one checkable open problem; no full solution is attributed to the Schottky/KP literature.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Baker function, tau ratio, and Miwa shifts
notes: \(\psi_W(g,z)=g(z)(1+\sum a_i(g)z^{-i})\in W\); multiplying by \(q_\zeta=1-z/\zeta\) gives its tau quotient and a vertex operator.
statement: Whenever \(g^{-1}W\to H_+\) is invertible, there is a unique Baker function with the stated asymptotic form and membership in \(W\). Its reduced form is \(\widetilde\psi_W(g,\zeta)=\tau_W(gq_\zeta)/\tau_W(g)\), \(|\zeta|>1\). If \(g=\exp(\sum t_i z^i)\), this is the shift \(t_i\mapsto t_i-1/(i\zeta^i)\), and hence a differential-exponential vertex-operator formula. The coefficients extend meromorphically through the tau zero set.
reconstruction: Uniqueness is first asserted on the big cell; the meromorphic extension does not give a finite regular Baker value at every tau zero.
fate: \citet[Proposition~5.1 and formulas~(5.14)--(5.16)]{segalwilson1985loop} provides the exact result.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Formal KP Lax operator and the Gelfand–Dikii reduction
notes: \(Q=D+\sum q_iD^{-i}\), \(\partial_{t_r}Q=[(Q^r)_+,Q]\); when \(Q^n=L\) is differential this becomes the \(n\)th KdV hierarchy. The condition is \(z^nW\subset W\).
statement: For the Baker dressing operator \(K=1+\sum a_iD^{-i}\), define \(Q=KDK^{-1}\). Then \(\partial_{t_r}Q=[(Q^r)_+,Q]\). If \((Q^n)_-=0\), the differential operator \(L=Q^n\) obeys \(\partial_{t_r}L=[(L^{r/n})_+,L]\). In the Grassmannian construction this reduction is precisely \(z^nW\subset W\). For \(L=D^2+u\), \(u=2\partial_x^2\log\tau\).
reconstruction: The positive part is taken after forming \(Q^r\). The factor 2 in the tau potential is required in the monic convention.
fate: \citet[Propositions~5.5 and 5.9, Corollary~5.12, eq.~(5.19)]{segalwilson1985loop} is the exact source. The hierarchy formalism itself is credited there to Sato and earlier Lax theory.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Pole-order bounds and regular singular scalar operators
notes: The notes say the resulting differential operator has only regular singular points in \(x\).
statement: For a Segal--Wilson solution and fixed remaining times, the Baker coefficient \(a_i(x)\) has poles of order at most \(i\). In the reduced order-\(n\) operator \(L=D^n+\sum_{i=0}^{n-2}u_iD^i\), each coefficient has pole order at most \(n-i\) at finite poles. Thus these finite singular points are regular singular in the scalar Fuchs criterion.
reconstruction: No assertion about regular singularity at infinity is added.
fate: \citet[Proposition~5.17 and Corollary~5.18 and their proofs in \S8]{segalwilson1985loop} proves precisely the finite-plane bounds.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: The determinant line and its nontrivial central extension
notes: \(\mathcal P\) is the frame bundle; \(\mathcal T\) is the trace-class change-of-frame group; pairs \((g,q)\) form \(\mathcal E\). Quotienting \(\mathcal E\) by \(\ker\det\) gives a central \(\mathbb C^*\)-extension acting on \(\mathrm{Det}\).
statement: The determinant line is associated to the admissible-frame bundle by the Fredholm determinant character of \(I+\mathcal L^1\). On the identity component of the restricted linear group, pairs \((g,q)\) with \(a q^{-1}-I\) trace class form an extension; quotienting by determinant-one frame transformations gives a central \(\mathbb C^*\)-extension. It acts on the determinant line, and generally does not admit a continuous global splitting.
reconstruction: The restricted operator ideals and the index-zero component are part of the definition; a lift is needed for the action on the line.
fate: \citet[\S3, especially the discussion preceding formula~(3.5)]{segalwilson1985loop} gives the nontrivial extension and its local cocycle.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Local Miura factorization and the flag of solutions
notes: \(D^2+u=(D-v)(D+v)\), \(u=v_x-v^2\); the general factorization is related to analytic initial values and meromorphic flags \(SL(n)/B\).
statement: Let \(L\) be monic of order \(n\) with analytic coefficients near an ordinary point and no \(D^{n-1}\) term. Complete flags in the \(n\)-dimensional local solution space determine factorizations into monic first order operators with meromorphic coefficients. Flags with all necessary initial Wronskians nonzero give analytic factors; they form an open chart with \(n(n-1)/2\) initial parameters. The second-order factorization obeys the stated Riccati relation.
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} This is local around an ordinary point; global meromorphic or periodic coefficients impose further monodromy constraints. The phrase every solution is not extended to global factorizations. The elementary identity is checked in the accompanying \nolinkurl{independent_checks.py}; this is a verification, not a novelty claim.
fate: \citet[\S3.7, Miura transformation]{drinfeldsokolov1985lie} supplies the hierarchy connection. The local flag statement follows from successive Wronskian factorization and explains the distinction drawn in the notebook.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Differential fields and the proposed Galois analogy
notes: The notes compare fields of coefficients, roots, and solutions, with \(B\) and \(SL(n)\) drawn beneath them, while observing that Miura fibres are not a group.
statement: The Picard--Vessiot differential Galois group is a subgroup of \(SL_n\) when the \(D^{n-1}\) coefficient vanishes; a complete solution flag has a stabilizer in a Borel subgroup. Which differential field is generated by a chosen factorization depends on the operator and flag. The diagram does not specify a universal equality of Galois groups or a question to prove.
fate: The Lie-theoretic Miura formalism of \citet[\S3]{drinfeldsokolov1985lie} is relevant background, but it is not an exact solution of an unstated differential-Galois problem.
present_status: As of November 2026, the analogy is meaningful but the notes do not fix one differential-field assertion.

title: The first KP coefficient and the two-time equation
notes: The note repeats \(Q=D+\sum q_iD^{-i}\), its Lax equations and the reduction, then says \(2q_1(x,t_2,t_3)\) solves KP.
statement: With \(x=t_1\), \(y=t_2\), \(t=t_3\) and \(u=2q_1\), the formal KP Lax equations imply \((4u_t-6uu_x-u_{xxx})_x=3u_{yy}\). The condition \(Q^n\) differential gives the Gelfand--Dikii reduction. Other signs result from explicit changes of time or leading-operator conventions.
reconstruction: The explicit PDE is supplied to make the coefficient assertion checkable; it is not written out on the source page.
fate: This is the same formalism as 1982-592.8, proved in \citet[\S5]{segalwilson1985loop}; the short conclusion does not introduce another new theorem.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Exact stationary phase and the fixed-component denominator
notes: For a compact symplectic manifold and Hamiltonian with compact or periodic flow, the notes write \(\int_M e^{iH}=\sum_j\operatorname{vol}(M_j)e^{iH(M_j)}/\lambda_j\), with \(\lambda_j\) a normal Pfaffian. The Fourier transform is said to have an exact stationary-phase answer.
statement: Let \((M^{2n},\omega)\) be compact and let a Hamiltonian circle action have generator \(\xi\), with \(\iota_\xi\omega=dH\). For the Cartan differential \(d+u\iota_\xi\), the equivariantly closed form is \(\omega-uH\). Localization gives \[\int_M e^{\omega-uH}=\sum_{F\subset M^{S^1}}\int_F\frac{e^{\omega_F-uH_F}}{e_{S^1}(\nu F)(u)}.\] Its left side means \(\int_M e^{-uH}\omega^n/n!\), with compatible Euler-class conventions. For isolated fixed points the denominators are products of weights and powers of \(u\). For positive-dimensional fixed components the full equivariant Euler class, including curvature terms, is needed.
reconstruction: The Liouville measure, deformation parameter, sign convention, and full fixed-component denominator are supplied. The notebook\textquotesingle s volume divided by a constant Pfaffian is not the unrestricted fixed-submanifold formula.
fate: The underlying theorem was published by \citet{duistermaatheckman1982variation} in 1982. \citet[\S\S3,6--7, especially formula~(3.8)]{atiyahbott1984moment}, received 20 December 1982 and published in 1984, gives this cohomological form and distinguishes isolated points from fixed submanifolds. Its bibliography records the 1982 Berline--Vergne and Duistermaat--Heckman addendum preprints.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Polynomial density on regular-value chambers
notes: The measure pushed forward by \(H\) is first called piecewise polynomial, then a polynomial on \(\mathbb R\). The reduced symplectic form is called linear in the level.
statement: For a compact Hamiltonian torus manifold, the pushforward of Liouville measure has a polynomial density on each chamber of regular values, relative to Lebesgue measure on the moment-map image. Under the natural local identification of reduced spaces, the cohomology class of the reduced symplectic form varies affinely with the moment value. This cohomological variation gives the polynomial volume; walls can change the polynomial.
reconstruction: Affineness concerns the reduced cohomology class after identification, not a global choice of local coordinate expressions for every reduced two-form.
fate: \citet{duistermaatheckman1982variation} is the 1982 source; \citet[\S7]{atiyahbott1984moment} gives the localization and Fourier-transform interpretation. This is not one polynomial valid across all critical values.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Gelfand’s question about stationary eigenvalues
notes: Gelfand remarks that the eigenvalues of the stationary action have not yet been used.
statement: The normal isotropy weights are precisely the linearized eigenvalue data entering the equivariant Euler denominator. No further proposed identity or missing conclusion is specified by the question.
fate: \citet[\S\S3 and 7]{atiyahbott1984moment} explains where those weights occur. The question is an expository challenge to the abbreviated derivation, not a separately identifiable unresolved theorem.
present_status: As of November 2026, the role of the normal weights is explicit in localization; no distinct open proposition is stated here.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Borel equivariant cohomology and localization
notes: \(H_G^*(M)=H^*(EG\times_GM)\), as a module over \(H^*(BG)\); for the circle \(H^*(BS^1;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q[u]\), \(\deg u=2\). Restriction to the fixed locus becomes an isomorphism over the fraction field. The notes recall Atiyah--Segal in K-theory and Quillen in cohomology.
statement: For a compact smooth circle manifold, restriction induces \[H_{S^1}^*(M;\mathbb Q)\otimes_{\mathbb Q[u]}\mathbb Q(u)\simeq H^*(M^{S^1};\mathbb Q)\otimes\mathbb Q(u).\] More generally a torus requires localization of its polynomial coefficient ring. The analogous statement for an arbitrary nonabelian compact group cannot be obtained just by replacing the circle fixed locus by the full group fixed locus.
reconstruction: Rational coefficients and the circle or torus restriction are explicit. A polynomial description of \(H^*(BG)\) needs the corresponding coefficient and compact-Lie-group hypotheses.
fate: \citet[\S\S2--3]{atiyahbott1984moment} reviews the earlier Borel/Atiyah--Segal localization and proves the integration formula. The lecture\textquotesingle s later explicit restriction to \(S^1\) supplies the relevant hypothesis.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: The invariant Cartan complex and the square of its differential
notes: \(d_1=d+u\iota_\xi\) is first written on all forms; the notes then insist on invariant forms from the start. They print \(d_1^2=u^2L_\xi\). Goncharov compares the construction with Chern--Weil theory.
statement: The Cartan model is \((\Omega(M)^{S^1}\otimes\mathbb C[u],d+u\iota_\xi)\), \(\deg u=2\). Cartan\textquotesingle s homotopy identity gives \((d+u\iota_\xi)^2=uL_\xi\), which vanishes on invariant forms. Its cohomology identifies with Borel equivariant cohomology over \(\mathbb C\); the Chern--Weil comparison uses a connection on the universal bundle.
reconstruction: The later correction to invariant forms is retained as part of the source argument, rather than counted as an unresolved omission.
fate: \citet[\S4]{atiyahbott1984moment} gives the differential-form model and its relation with the topological construction. The invariant-form qualification is already repaired in the notebook; only the extra power of \(u\) remains an actual formula error.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Parity localization and Vergne’s explicit contracting form
notes: After putting \(u=1\), the notes identify the parity cohomology with that of the fixed set. They first seek an invariant angular one-form \(\alpha\) with \(\iota_\xi\alpha=1\) and \(d\alpha=0\), then replace it by \(\beta=\alpha(1+d\alpha)^{-1}\) and write \(\omega=d_1(\beta\wedge\omega)+\beta\wedge d_1\omega\).
statement: On the complement of the zero set of a Killing field generating a compact action, choose an invariant metric and \(\alpha=\xi^\flat/\|\xi\|^2\). Then \(\iota_\xi\alpha=1\), \(L_\xi\alpha=0\). The finite exterior-algebra series \(\beta=\alpha\sum_{j\ge0}(-d\alpha)^j\) satisfies \((d+\iota_\xi)\beta=1\). Wedge multiplication by \(\beta\) contracts the invariant parity complex away from the fixed set. For compact \(M\), restriction therefore gives its \(\mathbb Z/2\)-graded cohomology as \(H^*(M^{S^1};\mathbb C)\) with parity grading; boundary integration near the fixed set yields the localization residues.
reconstruction: \ours{} A direct check is \(D\alpha=1+d\alpha\), \(D(d\alpha)=L_\xi\alpha-d(\iota_\xi\alpha)=0\); hence \(D\beta=1\), and the graded Leibniz rule gives the written identity. This verifies the recorded proof, not a new localization theorem. The earlier aspiration \(d\alpha=0\) is explicitly abandoned.
fate: \citet[\S\S4--5 and 8]{atiyahbott1984moment} treats this model and the relation to Witten and Berline--Vergne. Its reference [5] records the Rennes Berline--Vergne preprint of 1982, before this talk. The notebook itself contains the valid primitive and the contracting identity.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: A group-free formulation through the double fibration
notes: Gelfand asks to formulate the same theorem without \(G\), in the language of the two projections of \(EG\times_GM\).
statement: The diagram alone does not specify what structures should replace the group action, the polynomial coefficient ring, the fixed set, or the localization multiplicative set. Without those data it is not a single theorem about arbitrary double fibrations.
fate: The Borel and Cartan comparison in \citet[\S\S2--4]{atiyahbott1984moment} explains the diagram, but does not solve the additional unspecified group-free programme. No later groupoid or foliated theorem is treated as an exact answer.
present_status: As of November 2026, the wording remains insufficient to identify one falsifiable open problem.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Hamiltonian torus actions and the moment map
notes: The notes start with a compact symplectic torus manifold, then insert the assignment \(X\mapsto H_X\) compatible with Poisson brackets and define \(\mu(m)(X)=H_X(m)\).
statement: For a Hamiltonian action of a torus \(T\) on \((M,\omega)\), choose a linear assignment \(X\mapsto H_X\) with \(dH_X=\iota_{X_M}\omega\), compatible with the Lie and Poisson brackets. The map \(\mu:M\to\mathfrak t^*\) is defined by evaluation. A symplectic torus action need not be Hamiltonian; the inserted Hamiltonian assignment is an essential assumption.
reconstruction: The inserted Poisson representation is treated as part of the notes, not silently supplied by symplecticity alone.
fate: \citet[\S1]{atiyah1982convexity} states the Hamiltonian setup before the convexity theorem. This continues the moment-map discussion in 1981-556.12 and 1980-508.15; it is not the exact orbital-integral question of 1982-568.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Convexity of the moment image
notes: \(\mu(M)\) is asserted to be a convex polytope; the margin credits Atiyah--Bott and Guillemin--Sternberg independently.
statement: If a torus acts in a Hamiltonian manner on a compact connected symplectic manifold, its moment-map image is the convex hull of the finitely many images of connected fixed-point components, and its fibres are connected. Compactness and connectedness are part of the theorem.
reconstruction: The connected-fibre conclusion is included to identify Atiyah\textquotesingle s precise theorem, although it is not separately stated in this short note.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1]{atiyah1982convexity}, received 27 March 1981 and published in 1982, proves this theorem. The independent convexity work is by Guillemin--Sternberg, as also described in \citet[\S6]{atiyahbott1984moment}; the source margin conflates Atiyah\textquotesingle s convexity paper with the joint equivariant-localization work.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Critical walls and the Duistermaat–Heckman density
notes: The density is piecewise polynomial on \(\mu(M)\); transitions are called faces where \(d\mu\) degenerates and are said to lie in planes.
statement: The moment-map critical values lie in finitely many affine subspaces coming from isotropy strata. The regular-value chambers carry polynomial Duistermaat--Heckman densities. Critical walls may occur in the interior of the moment polytope; they are not restricted to its boundary faces.
reconstruction: The word faces is read as a wall decomposition, not as an assertion that every critical value belongs to the boundary of the image.
fate: This is the torus version of 1982-593.2. \citet{duistermaatheckman1982variation} and \citet[\S\S6--7]{atiyahbott1984moment} supply the precise chamber picture.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Special-value programme and the limits of the surviving statement
notes: The heading distinguishes formulations modulo \(\mathbb Q^*\) from exact formulations, followed by the name Birch--Swinnerton-Dyer.
statement: The notes contain no regulator map, motivic cohomology group, rank equality, leading coefficient, or specified integer special value. They announce a programme rather than state a precise special-value conjecture.
fate: The modern distinctions between Hasse--Weil continuation and stronger arithmetic conjectures are reviewed in \citet[\S1]{gee2026modularity}. The earlier regulator occurrence 1979-476.11 is related context, not an exact recurrence inferable from this heading.
present_status: As of November 2026, no particular regulator or Birch--Swinnerton-Dyer formula can be identified from this entry alone.

title: Arithmetic models and the local point-count zeta function
notes: The notes choose equations supposedly giving smooth reduction at every prime, write \(\zeta(X,s)=\prod_p\zeta(X_{\mathbb F_p},s)\), and define each local factor by \(\sum_n\#X(\mathbb F_{p^n})p^{-ns}\). The point example then gives the usual Riemann Euler product.
statement: For a smooth projective geometrically connected curve \(X/\mathbb Q\), there is a smooth proper model over \(\mathbb Z[1/S]\) for a finite set of bad primes \(S\); changing equations cannot generally remove bad reduction. At a good prime, \[Z(X_p,t)=\exp\!\left(\sum_{n\ge1}\#X_p(\mathbb F_{p^n})\frac{t^n}{n}\right),\qquad t=p^{-s}.\] Bad local factors require the chosen arithmetic zeta or cohomological L-function convention. A point has \(Z(t)=(1-t)^{-1}\); the unexponentiated series is the logarithmic derivative data, not the local zeta function.
reconstruction: The finite bad set, exponential, and divisor \(n\) are indispensable. The word rational in the margin is not interpreted as a genus-zero hypothesis because the continuation discussion explicitly addresses general curves.
fate: \citet[\S1]{deligne1974weil} gives the finite-field zeta and cohomological factors. \citet[\S1.1]{boxercalegarigeepilloni2021surfaces} explicitly separates the global Euler product and finitely many excluded factors.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Weil rationality and the correct location of finite-field zeros
notes: The local function is rational in \(p^{-s}\), with numerator and denominator factors; a damaged formula places zeros at \(\operatorname{Re}z=p^{?/2}\). The notes remark that the curve case is proved.
statement: For a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus \(g\) over \(\mathbb F_p\), \[Z(X,t)=\frac{\prod_{j=1}^{2g}(1-\alpha_jt)}{(1-t)(1-pt)},\qquad |\alpha_j|=p^{1/2}.\] Thus the numerator zeros in the \(t\)-plane have modulus \(p^{-1/2}\); in the variable \(t=p^{-s}\), they lie on \(\Re s=1/2\). These statements concern a local finite-field factor, not the global Riemann hypothesis.
reconstruction: The damaged exponent is not guessed. The three distinct variables---Frobenius eigenvalue, local zero, and complex s---are separated.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1.6]{deligne1974weil} proves purity in every cohomological degree for smooth projective varieties, not merely curves. The paper records July 1973 lectures and was published in 1974; both precede this 1983 exposition.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Which coefficients define reasonable Euler factors?
notes: Gelfand asks which \(a_n(p)\) in \(\prod_p\sum_n a_n(p)p^{-ns}\) should be called reasonable, observing that \(a_n(p)=1\) for the Riemann zeta function.
statement: The question does not impose local rationality, integrality, purity, conductor bounds, compatibility across primes, or an automorphic or motivic origin. These choices give inequivalent classification problems.
fate: \citet[\S1]{gee2026modularity} specifies the geometric and Galois data in a modern Hasse--Weil question. It does not supply a necessary-and-sufficient characterization of the undefined word reasonable.
present_status: As of November 2026, the wording does not identify one precise open classification problem.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Global continuation and functional equations for curves
notes: The notes say analytic continuation is not proved even for curves over \(\mathbb Q\), contrast the finite-field case, and locate the obstacle in compatibility among different primes.
statement: For every smooth projective geometrically connected curve over \(\mathbb Q\), prove meromorphic continuation of its completed arithmetic zeta function and the expected functional equation, with the local bad factors and archimedean factors specified. Equivalently, one may formulate continuation for the Hasse--Weil L-function of its \(H^1\), after separating the Tate factors. This is a global assertion; finite-field rationality alone does not imply it.
reconstruction: The precise completion and the distinction between the arithmetic zeta function and its \(H^1\) L-factor are supplied. The historical sentence is read as a general conjecture, not as denying all previously known special curves.
fate: For genus one over \(\mathbb Q\), \citet[Theorem~A]{breuilconraddiamondtaylor2001modularity} proves modularity and hence the analytic assertion (2001). For every genus-two curve over a totally real field, \citet[Theorem~1.1.2]{boxercalegarigeepilloni2021surfaces} proves meromorphic continuation and the functional equation, by potential automorphy in Theorem~1.1.3. Their work circulated at the end of 2018, was received 25 December 2018, and appeared in 2021. \citet[\S1 and Remark~2.7]{gee2026modularity} gives the November 2026 research perspective.
present_status: As of November 2026, the unrestricted curve statement remains open. Genus one over \(\mathbb Q\) and genus two over totally real fields have the stated continuation results. Potential automorphy gives meromorphic continuation over the original field; it does not establish holomorphy of every genus-two \(H^1\) L-function.
worth: Worth pursuing in explicit higher-genus families because general global continuation remains unresolved and local point-count data alone do not control the Euler product.

title: Matching geometric H1 factors with automorphic L-functions
notes: A strong conjecture says the two classes of geometric zeta functions and Langlands zeta functions coincide.
statement: A precise direction relevant to a curve is that the compatible Galois representations on its \(H^1\) should correspond to suitable algebraic automorphic data, allowing isobaric decompositions when the motive is reducible, with matching good Euler factors and compatible completions. Literal equality with every automorphic L-function is too broad: algebraicity, weight, and motivic constraints matter.
reconstruction: The formulation is one modern geometric-to-automorphic direction extracted from the broad notebook sentence, not a claim that the notes formulated a complete Langlands reciprocity conjecture.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1.1.3]{boxercalegarigeepilloni2021surfaces} gives potential automorphy for all genus-two curves over totally real fields. Stronger actual modularity is proved under explicit extra hypotheses by \citet[Theorem~B]{boxercalegarigeepilloni2025modularity}: for a genus-two curve \(y^2=f(x)\) over \(\mathbb Q\), \(\deg f=5\), surjective mod 3 representation on its Jacobian and good ordinary reduction at 2 and 3 imply modularity. The preprint was posted 28 February 2025. \citet[Remark~2.7]{gee2026modularity} places this advance in the continuing programme.
present_status: As of November 2026, general actual automorphy for arbitrary curve \(H^1\) remains open. The 2025 theorem has the stated genus-two, rational-Weierstrass-point, residual-image and ordinary-reduction hypotheses; it is not modularity of every abelian surface.
worth: Worth developing for carefully specified motives or explicit curves because actual automorphy is stronger than potential automorphy and can yield holomorphy as well as continuation.

title: The elliptic completion and what the BSD heading does not say
notes: Under the resumed Birch--Swinnerton-Dyer heading, only continuation and symmetry of \((2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)\zeta(X,s)\) under \(s\mapsto2-s\) are written; the strip \(0\le\Re s\le2\) is drawn.
statement: For an elliptic curve \(E/\mathbb Q\) with conductor \(N\), the completed Hasse--Weil L-function is \(\Lambda(E,s)=N^{s/2}(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)L(E,s)\), and \(\Lambda(E,s)=w_E\Lambda(E,2-s)\), where \(w_E\in\{\pm1\}\). The whole arithmetic zeta function of the curve contains additional Tate factors and has a different completion. Neither the equality of analytic and algebraic ranks nor the BSD leading-term formula appears in these notes.
reconstruction: The conductor, root number, and identification of the displayed series with \(L(H^1(E),s)\) are necessary emendations; genus one is inferred from the single gamma factor and the named conjecture, with that inference made explicit.
fate: \citet[Theorem~A]{breuilconraddiamondtaylor2001modularity} establishes modularity of every elliptic curve over \(\mathbb Q\), hence the continuation and functional equation written here after these corrections. The broader BSD conjecture is not thereby solved and is not manufactured as a separate occurrence.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Dedekind zeta and Shintani cone series
notes: Wodzicki asks which zeta functions can be computed and cites Shintani, writing \(\zeta_K(s)=\sum_{\mathfrak a}N\mathfrak a^{-s}=\sum_n a_n n^{-s}\).
statement: For a number field \(K\), the sum is over nonzero integral ideals, \(N\mathfrak a=|\mathcal O_K/\mathfrak a|\), and converges for \(\Re s>1\). For totally real \(K\), Shintani\textquotesingle s cone decomposition expresses partial Dedekind zeta functions as finite sums of shifted positive-cone Dirichlet series associated with products of real linear forms; these yield values at nonpositive integers. The totally real assumption belongs to this particular construction.
reconstruction: The nonzero-integral-ideal condition and totally real scope are supplied; the notes do not specify which special values or which field signature.
fate: \citet[opening pages and \S1]{cassounogues1982series} explicitly states Shintani\textquotesingle s 1976 result and develops the associated polynomial Dirichlet series. It was a 1981 arithmetic-days report, published in 1982, before this talk. The original 1976 paper\textquotesingle s bibliographic identity is confirmed by that primary research account; its full text was not obtained here.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result with the hypotheses stated above.

title: Constant-coefficient operators on a torus: unresolved identification
notes: The Shintani construction is described as reducing the Dedekind zeta function to zeta functions of pseudodifferential operators on a torus with constant coefficients.
statement: A cone-restricted polynomial lattice sum can be viewed formally as a spectral sum after choosing a Fourier multiplier and a projection onto a cone of modes. That does not by itself make it the zeta function of an ordinary positive classical elliptic operator on the whole torus. The symbol, ellipticity, multiplicities, cone projection and zero-mode convention must be specified.
reconstruction: The Fourier-multiplier interpretation is supplied only to explain what additional data an exact statement would require, and is not claimed as a recovered historical theorem.
fate: The primary account \citet{cassounogues1982series} verifies the cone Dirichlet series but does not identify the unrestricted torus pseudodifferential assertion written here. Searches combining Shintani, Dedekind zeta, torus, constant coefficients and pseudodifferential operators did not locate an exact operator theorem. This is an unresolved identification, not evidence that the arithmetic method was undeveloped.
present_status: As of November 2026, the Shintani arithmetic construction is established; the exact operator realization intended by the note has not been identified.
